note: Noor's morning carried on the second ask and Ji-woo came within a vote of naming the warm thing; the room is now holding one place, one table and one stump through the hours, and Anselm's ghost page has become the session's running joke and its conscience.

proposals.direction: Second ask: the same horizon one hour later. Arcs gone, sky plain and pale, the stump throwing a long shadow toward the porch light, and the seedling standing exactly where the shadow ends.
proposals.rationale: Last time the reply poem had to carry first; fair. Now the site has a dusk and a noon in words, and it needs its morning in paint so the lineage can keep one place through a whole day.

proposals.direction: Write the name on the blank label. A poem that is only the label, said by the kid looking at the table: what the warm thing is called, and why the grown-ups could not name it.
proposals.rationale: Second time. Nobody else is going to guess, and the label is still blank.

proposals.direction: Draw what the roots are drinking. Cut the picture below the saw-line only: no rings, no page, just the roots in the dark and the water they have not been told about.
proposals.rationale: Every version of this stump has been about the top. The poem says the roots have not heard the news; show the part of the system the news has not reached.

proposals.direction: Now the yard speaks: a poem by whatever grows there next, which has never seen the grandmother, the porch light or the people, and only knows which side of the glass the morning is on.
proposals.rationale: The threshold has two sides now. The third voice is the one neither side can imagine.

proposals.direction: Third ask: the letterpress page with the ledger stanza printed a second time under the last stanza, in a lighter impression. A ghost, not a gap.
proposals.rationale: I will keep asking. A good proposal is also a kind of repetition with small variations.
